card.title: No. 9 COMMANDO
card.text: Deployment: Set the defense of target enemy unit to 1.
card.flavorText: No. 9 Commando was a battalion sized unit raised from volunteers by the British Army during WWII.  Their first raid, Operation Sunstar, took place on the night of 22/23 November- 1941 on the French coast at Houlgate and was concluded successfully with no casualties. In March 1942, No. 9 Commando participated in the Saint-Nazaire Raid, providing demolition support alongside other commando units, such as No. 2 Commando. Later that year they reinforced the Gibraltar garrison during Operation Torch, the Allied landings in French North Africa. Following this, they conducted raids on the Italian islands of Tremiti and Pianosa. During the Allied invasion of Italy, as part of the 2nd Special Service Brigade, they engaged in Operation Partridge in December 1943 around the Garigliano River. Then they took part in Operation Shingle, the Anzio landings, and saw combat at Monte Ornito, which led to their withdrawal to Naples in March 1944. Later that year, No. 9 Commando participated in Operation Darlington in May, aimed at rescuing Allied POWs located in Italy, and Operation Gradient in August, which involved demolishing a bridge in the Northern Adriatic. They later operated in Greece before returning to Italy, engaging in Operation Roast, the crossing of Comacchio Lagoon, and finally the battle of the Argenta Gap in April 1945. After the end of WWII, the unit was disbanded in 1946.
